title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-10-09
ranking_explanation: Repositories are ordered by stars gained in the GitHub Trending daily view captured at 2026-10-09 00:25 UTC. Total stars and default-branch commit SHAs were corroborated via GitHub REST API.
global_caveat: Daily star velocity measures attention, not adoption or project maturity. Repository metadata can move between the Trending page render and API reads.

themes.title: Agent workflows and context
themes.content: REA, mattpocock/skills, claude-mem, and anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins show demand for agents that use domain-specific tools, follow reusable processes, and retain useful context.

themes.title: Visual authoring for people and agents
themes.content: diagram-design targets structured technical communication, while ArtCraft offers hands-on 2D/3D controls for generative media.

themes.title: Reverse engineering and platform interoperability
themes.content: REA and AnyPS5 lead attention in analysis and compatibility tooling; RAD Debugger is a conventional native-debugging counterpoint.

themes.title: Learning and reference
themes.content: system-design-notes represents a practical interview-preparation/reference resource rather than a software tool.

themes.title: Languages
themes.content: TypeScript leads the listed set with two repositories. HTML, Rust, Shell, C++, C, and Python each appear once; one repository has no primary language listed by GitHub.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-powered reverse engineering leads today's list, with REA gaining the most stars in this snapshot (+7,738). Strong secondary signals come from PS5-to-PC porting, agent-oriented visual design, and reusable engineering skills.

sections.title: morluto/rea
sections.description: An MCP and CLI toolkit for agent-assisted reverse engineering of binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.
sections.why_notable: Largest daily gain in the captured Trending list; its README emphasizes local analysis with evidence and limitations surfaced to the user.
sections.unique_caveat: Native analysis can depend on a configured Hopper or Ghidra provider; the README says static JavaScript analysis needs neither engine.

sections.title: boykopovar/AnyPS5
sections.description: A tool for porting PS5 executables to Linux and Windows without emulation or a separate runtime process.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain; its README describes a relinker and system-library implementations, making console compatibility and preservation a major non-agent story today.
sections.unique_caveat: The project README points users to a game compatibility list and says unsupported states terminate with an error.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: Editorial diagram types and self-contained HTML/SVG output for coding agents and compatible hosts.
sections.why_notable: A large design-tool signal; its README highlights static, build-free output and separates semantic patterns from layout grammar.
sections.unique_caveat: README describes static HTML as the default; optional motion is available for ordered explanations.

sections.title: storytold/artcraft
sections.description: A visual IDE for interactive AI image and video creation.
sections.why_notable: One of the day's strongest creative-tool gains; README examples focus on 2D/3D compositing, scene blocking, camera placement, and controllable generation.
sections.unique_caveat: README links to a downloadable app as well as build-from-source instructions; this snapshot does not assess model/provider availability.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: A collection of small, composable agent skills for software engineering and productivity workflows.
sections.why_notable: Prominent agent-workflow entry by total audience; its README pitches adaptable, cross-model skills rather than a single end-to-end process framework.
sections.unique_caveat: The README distinguishes install/update behavior by agent host and warns against installing both a plugin and editable copy of the same skills.

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: Persistent context across sessions, with captured work compressed and retrieved into later agent sessions.
sections.why_notable: Adds durable memory to the agent-tooling cluster and explicitly targets interoperability across several coding agents.
sections.unique_caveat: Repository description claims support across multiple agent hosts; this report does not independently test that compatibility.

sections.title: liquidslr/system-design-notes
sections.description: Community notes covering system-design interview topics and case studies.
sections.why_notable: Learning/reference project among today's faster risers; README organizes notes around scaling, distributed systems, and common design exercises.
sections.unique_caveat: GitHub's repository API reports last push 2026-08-12; today's signal is attention rather than fresh code activity. README says the notes are a work in progress.

sections.title: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins
sections.description: Role-oriented plugins bundling skills, connectors, commands, and sub-agents for knowledge work.
sections.why_notable: A concrete packaging pattern for workplace agents, pairing role-specific workflows with integrations and customization points.
sections.unique_caveat: README says the plugins are built for Claude Cowork and compatible with Claude Code; compatibility beyond those hosts is not claimed here.

sections.title: EpicGames/raddebugger
sections.description: A native, user-mode, multi-process graphical debugger.
sections.why_notable: A lower-ranked but useful counterpoint to the agent-heavy list; its README identifies it as alpha and currently Windows x64/PDB-focused.
sections.unique_caveat: README identifies the project as alpha and currently limited to local Windows x64 debugging with PDBs.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflows/context (REA, mattpocock/skills, claude-mem, knowledge-work-plugins); visual authoring (diagram-design, ArtCraft); reverse engineering/interoperability (REA, AnyPS5, RAD Debugger). Languages across nine entries: TypeScript 2; HTML, Rust, Shell, C++, C, and Python 1 each; one N/A.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The clearest through-line is a shift from chat-only agents toward tools that let agents inspect software, follow reusable procedures, preserve context, and connect to work systems. Yet the day's biggest signals are not exclusively AI: AnyPS5 and the debugger show interest in compatibility and lower-level software, while creative tooling is also rising. Daily star velocity measures attention, not adoption or project maturity.
